title: CHEM 3.1 & 3.2 Review
subject: Chemistry
body:
Lesson 3.1 (The Philosophers):

1. Democritus's Ideas (Greek):
  • Matter is not infinitely divisible.
  • Matter is made of atoms that float in empty space
  • Atoms are homogeneous, indivisible, and are different from each other in size & shape.
2. Aristotle's Ideas (Greek):
  • Empty space doesn't exist
  • Matter is made of earth, fire, air, and water.
3. John Dalton's Ideas - Dalton's Postulates (English):
  • Agreed with Democritus in some ways: Matter is made of atoms which are indivisible.
  • Atoms of a given element have identical size, mass, and chemical properties
  • Atoms of one element are diff. from those of other elements.
  • Diff. elements combine in whole # ratios called compounds
  • In chemical reactions, atoms are separated, combines, or rearranged.
  • Dalton's Atomic Theory: The Law of Conservation of Mass - atoms aren't created/destroyed, they are rearranged.
Lesson 3.2 (Defining the Atom):
Atom: Smallest particle of matter that retains the properties of the element.
The Scanning Tunneling Model (STM) was used to visualize atoms.
Electron:
  • In 1860, Cathode Ray Tube was invented and was discovered by Sir William Crookes. There is a battery, two metal electrodes (wires) are connected to the battery and to the two ends of the vacuum tube. The negative side is called the cathode. The positive side is anode. A (-) charged particle was placed near the tube and the light repelled so this showed that the ray was (-) charged or made of electrons.
  • J.J. Thompson discovered in 1890 that John Dalton was WRONG: atoms were divisible into smaller particles called subatomic particles. Thompson was the one who discovered the electron.
Plum Pudding Model (by J.J. Thompson): The atom is (+) with (-) charged particles scattered around, and the (+) and (-) cancel out, so the atom is neutral.
Robert Millikan (American) discovered electron charge: 1-, and mass: 9.1 × 10^{-28}
Nucleus:
Ernest Rutherford: Concluded that the Plum Pudding Model was WRONG! He concluded this when he aimed alpha particles (protons) at a sheet of gold foil surrounded by a screen. Most passed through without deflecting, some deflected though. If the whole atom were positive (like in the Plum Pudding Model), all the particles would have deflected because like charges (the alpha particles and the surrounding area) repel.
He concluded:
  • Atoms are mostly made of empty space where electrons live
  • All of the (+) particles and mass is contained in the center of the nucleus.
His model: A (+) charged nucleus surrounded by (-) electrons. Alpha (+) particles/protons far from nucleus deflect only a little, but the ones passing near the nucleus deflect more.
The Proton and the Neutron:
  • 1920: Ernest Rutherford said nucleus included protons (charge: 1+).
  • 1932: James Chadwick: the nucleus ALSO has neutron (neutral charge), it has equal mass to the proton.
Properties of Subatomic Particles:
Electron: e^{-} (Symbol), 1- (charge), \frac{1}{84} (relative mass), 9.1 × 10^{-28} (real mass)
Proton: p, 1+, 1, 1.673 × 10^{-24}
Neutron: n, 0, 1, 1.675 × 10^{-24}
